title: Why one dollar buys two different lives
description:
One American dollar buys about eight dollars worth of life in Nigeria. This short maps the price level ratio, the number that shows what your money actually buys once prices are local.

The World Bank measures the spread as a price level ratio. The United States is the reference at 1.000. The United Kingdom is 0.89, Germany 0.80, Japan 0.65, Mexico 0.54, India 0.23 and Nigeria 0.128. That is a 7.8 times gap between the highest and lowest economy in this set. Figures are real published data for 2025, the latest available release. The two numbers are both correct and answer different questions: an exchange rate is a trade quote, a price level is a shopping list.

Sources:
World Bank, World Development Indicators, GDP per capita (current US$), NY.GDP.PCAP.CD, 2025: https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/all/indicator/NY.GDP.PCAP.CD?format=json&date=2021:2025
World Bank, World Development Indicators, GDP per capita, PPP (constant 2021 international $), NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.CD, 2025: https://api.worldbank.org/v2/country/all/indicator/NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.CD?format=json&date=2021:2025
Map boundaries: Natural Earth 10m (public domain).

Illustrative values and shapes are labelled on screen in the video.
